candidates.detail: Public RiggedMesh exposes body positions and normals as raw f32 rows. The export input validator checks nonzero matching row counts, rig/index relationships and weight sums, and separately checks shell positions and normals for finiteness, but it does not check body normal components for finiteness. The exporter serializes every body normal with f32::to_le_bytes into a buffer view and, when export_body is true, exposes that complete view as a float VEC3 NORMAL accessor. A body normal containing NaN therefore reaches that native buffer if the remaining export and write steps succeed. Khronos glTF 2.0 accessor rules prohibit NaN and infinities. No input, export, file, glTF validator, rendering or product code ran.
candidates.input_and_path: For a source-only witness, take the exporter source fixture with its finite three-vertex body, valid indexed face and attachment skeleton; append a fourth finite position with a matching valid skin row and append a normal containing NaN for that unused vertex, retaining the original face and other rows. The inspected checks depend on row lengths, face bounds, skin and rig fields rather than the body normal values. Empty morph and shell inputs avoid unrelated shell checks. The original attachment geometry is unchanged because the face still references only the original three vertices. If all later geometry, serialization and filesystem operations succeed, the fourth normal still lies in the exported NORMAL accessor. The fixture and this modification are reasoning aids only; neither was run or shown to occur in production.
candidates.consumer_and_safeguards: The offline-creator feature gates the public export module. Shell positions and normals, morph deltas and socket transforms have separate finite checks, and the current GLB writer checks native lengths before its GLB write; those safeguards do not inspect body normal components. Actual model generation, other consumers and additional body or rig finite contracts require independent discovery.
candidates.connected_scope: Source body and rig admission, RiggedMesh and exported POSITION/NORMAL data, native glTF accessor and bounds, shell/morph and skin correspondence, exporter error propagation and actual model producer policy.
candidates.proposed_repair: After exhaustive discovery and separate implementation authorization, establish one finite geometry contract at the earliest appropriate body/export boundary and reject nonfinite values with contextual errors before native serialization. Trace all relevant body, rig and morph channels while preserving valid export geometry, supported levels of detail, skin and existing checked framing.
candidates.later_acceptance: When product validation is authorized, show nonfinite body normal and other admitted native geometry channels fail before invalid output, ordinary finite body and shell exports remain valid, and the declared producer and native glTF contract agree.
